input: Track my daily water intake for one month

keyUnknowns.whyItMatters: Knowing whether the goal is to hit a specific daily target (e.g. 2L, 8 glasses) vs. simply observe patterns changes what counts as success and what to measure.
Whether the user wants a phone app, a spreadsheet, a paper log, or a smart bottle determines the entire tracking system to set up.
Knowing when they plan to log (in the moment, end of day, etc.) affects how reminders and the logging workflow should be structured.
Whether only plain water counts or all fluids (coffee, tea, juice, etc.) directly changes what needs to be recorded each entry.
How much friction the user is willing to accept (e.g. manual entry every sip vs. a simple daily tally) determines the complexity of the system.
Whether this is purely personal or shared with a doctor, coach, or accountability partner affects the level of detail and format of records needed.
Preferred units (ml, oz, cups, glasses) and how results are reviewed (daily summary, weekly chart, etc.) shapes how data is recorded and displayed.

gold.taskTitle: Track daily water intake for one month
gold.taskDescription: The user wants to monitor how much water they drink each day over a 30-day period.

questions.title: What is your target amount of water per day?
questions.description: Does the user have a specific daily goal in mind (e.g. 2 litres, 8 glasses), or are they tracking to discover their baseline with no fixed target yet?

questions.title: Which tool do you want to use for logging?
questions.description: Should the plan be built around a phone app, a spreadsheet, a paper journal, a smart water bottle, or another method?

questions.title: When during the day will you record each entry?
questions.description: Will the user log in real time after each drink, at set intervals, or in a single recap at the end of the day?

questions.title: Should only plain water count, or all fluids?
questions.description: Clarifies whether coffee, tea, juice, soups, or other beverages should be included in the daily total or excluded.

questions.title: How much effort are you willing to put into logging?
questions.description: Does the user want a quick, low-friction daily total, or are they comfortable with detailed per-drink entries throughout the day?

questions.title: Is this tracking just for yourself or shared with someone?
questions.description: Will the data be reviewed only by the user, or does it need to be shared with a doctor, nutritionist, or accountability partner?

questions.title: Which units and review format do you prefer?
questions.description: Does the user think in millilitres, ounces, cups, or glasses, and do they want to review progress as a daily number, a weekly chart, or a monthly summary?
